question: Along its course, River ________ passes through Tibet, where it is known as Tsangpo, and also passes through the Indian states of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Bangladesh.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​__The Brahmaputra River passes through Tibet, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Bangladesh: 
 
• The Brahmaputra forms the world's largest number of freshwater riverine islands, including Majuli, the world's largest freshwater riverine island.
 
• The Brahmaputra is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet.
 
• It originates in the Chemayungdung glacier in the Himalayas near Mount Kailash.
 
• The Brahmaputra flows through the Indian states of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam.
 
• In Assamese, it is known as Brahmaputra or Luit.
 
• The Brahmaputra is known as the Jamuna in Bangladesh. 
 
• It joins the Ganga in Bangladesh and eventually drains into the Bay of Bengal. 
 
• Other names
 
• The Brahmaputra is also known as the Siang/Dihang River in Arunachali.
 
• The word "Brahmaputra" means "son of Brahma" in Sanskrit
 
• The Brahmaputra is India's largest river by volume.
 
• It has one of the largest river basins in South Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Ramganga River
 
• Origin: The Ramganga River originates from the Doodhatoli ranges in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• Flow:
 
• It flows southeast through the Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand.
 
• Then, it enters Uttar Pradesh and passes through cities like Moradabad, Bareilly, and Badaun.
 
• Finally, it merges into the Ganga River near Kannauj in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Brahmani River
 
• Origin: The Brahmani River is formed by the confluence of the Koel and Sankh Rivers near Rourkela in Odisha, India.
 
• Flow:
 
• It flows eastward through Odisha.
 
• Major cities and regions along its course include Angul, Talcher, and Dhenkanal.
 
• It eventually drains into the Bay of Bengal near Dhamra in Odisha.
 
• Mahanadi River
 
• Origin: The Mahanadi River originates from the Sihawa Hills in the Dhamtari district of Chhattisgarh, India.
 
• Flow:
 
• It flows eastward through Chhattisgarh and Odisha, covering major cities like Raipur, Cuttack, and Sambalpur.
 
• The river forms an extensive delta before emptying into the Bay of Bengal near Paradeep in Odisha.
 
• It is also known for the Hirakud Dam, one of the largest dams in India.
